subject: URGENT: Throughput regression and 500s — suspected KV cache lock contention
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@brightcart.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 99p latency + 500s across inference endpoints

Hi Rachel / Monica,

We're seeing a severe regression this morning: our production routes to the Redwood inference endpoint (model: seq-1.4) are returning intermittent 500s and p99 latency has jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s across multiple regions. Errors started around 07:50 PDT and have been impacting checkout personalization (order flow) — we're currently seeing ~8% error rate on user-facing requests.

We collected a short trace and a few sample request IDs (attached). Can someone confirm whether this looks like a service-side problem or something in our integration? This is blocking our peak window.

Sanjay
Ops Lead, BrightCart

Subject: Re: Spike in 99p latency + 500s across inference endpoints

Quick findings from the first-look triage (logs attached: kv_stats_snapshot_20260914.txt, perf_log_20260913.zip):

- Correlation: Errors and tail latency align with sustained KV cache mutex contention on the tenant's hot prefix (prefix_id: bc_promos).
- Symptoms observed: rapid short-lived cache thrash (high insert/evict rate), long lock-waits on KV shard mutex (95th percentile lock wait ~720ms), and sudden backlog in upstream request queues leading to HOL blocking at the runtime batching layer.
- Impact: When the KV lock blocks, in-flight requests stall waiting for prefix state; downstream batching waits push latency over timeout thresholds which surface as 500s and token-generation stalls.

Hypothesis: a workload shift (BrightCart heavy A/B personalization tests) bumped access skew to a small set of prefixes. Our current KV config for tenant isolation uses a coarse-grained mutex per prefix which becomes contended under extremely hot prefix access. The runtime's continuous batching then exacerbates HOL blocking when one request holds the lock while others build up in the batch.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:00–10:20 PDT):
- Bypassed KV prefix locking for read-only cache hits on the affected prefix (experimental path) — reduced lock wait p95 to ~80ms in the short window.
- Increased batching soft timeout to drain queued requests faster where safe.

Next steps (I propose):
1) Short term (hours): keep the read-bypass enabled and monitor error rate; deploy a hot-prefix rate limiter for the tenant to bound burst.
2) Medium term (days): implement finer-grained sharding for the prefix mutex (split by prefix shard key) + add per-tenant hot-shard backpressure to prevent HOL collapse.
3) Post-mortem: capture a reproducible stress test (BrightCart dataset or synthetic) to validate shard/lock changes before wide rollout.

I've attached heap_snapshot_0914.txt and the kv stats. Will follow up with a timeline for a patch.

Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv_stats_snapshot_20260914.txt, perf_log_20260913.zip, heap_snapshot_0914.txt
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@brightcart.com>

Appreciate the rapid response and the temporary bypass — we've seen error rate drop to ~1.2% after 10:15, p99 trending down. However, the issue recurred briefly at 10:48 when we resumed a larger A/B cohort. We urgently need a safe throttling approach — we can't risk a full checkout outage during peak.

Can Redwood place a tenant-level burst cap or a per-prefix soft-queue limit immediately while you build the finer-grained lock sharding? Otherwise we'll have to roll back the test.

Sanjay
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Executive summary & action plan — BrightCart outage window (14 Sep)

Markus / Leadership,

Summary: BrightCart experienced an availability/latency regression tied to KV cache lock contention on a very hot prefix (bc_promos) which caused HOL blocking at the runtime batching layer and surfaced as elevated p99 and 500s. Marcus validated the hypothesis and applied a temporary read-bypass that reduced error rates. The problem partially recurred under a larger burst.

Immediate ask (0–4 hours):
- Approve tenant-level burst cap for BrightCart (soft throttle at 120 RPS sustained per hot-prefix) to be deployed as a fail-safe. Marcus can implement a circuit that returns a 429 before requests enter the hot-path.
- Authorize a controlled rollback window for BrightCart's A/B cohort if we observe >2% errors in the next 2 hours.

Engineering next steps (24–72 hours):
- Marcus: ship fine-grained prefix mutex sharding + forced backpressure on hot shards (INF-7821). Target: 48h for canary patch and 72h for broader rollout if stable.
- Monica: expand observability with a hot-prefix heatmap and automated anomaly alerting tied to eviction/lock metrics.
- Rachel: coordinate a joint runbook with BrightCart for safer staged rollouts.

I'll escalate to Sales leadership and coordinate a customer update call at 18:00 PDT with BrightCart. Please reply with any objections to the above mitigation plan within 30 minutes.

Rachel Kim
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
